questions.question: For the sample checkout-api rollout, which score does root_cause assign to the bad-rollout hypothesis?
options: 0.500, because all hypotheses receive the same starting score
0.090, because only the DNS hypothesis has a numeric score
0.735, using the recent revision, two telemetry citations, specificity 0.82, and path length 0
0.140, because the Prometheus error rate is 0.14
questions.explanation: The sample scoring function combines recency, specificity, capped citation count, and path weight; the printed bad-rollout score is 0.735.

questions.question: Which hypothesis is ranked first for Deployment/checkout-api in the sample graph?
options: DNS flap in kube-system/coredns
node-level pressure on ip-10-2-3-4
a stale Service selector on checkout-api
bad rollout: image checkout-api:v2.41 fails /healthz
questions.explanation: The recently deployed v2.41 image is linked to both Prometheus and Loki evidence, so its bad-rollout hypothesis outranks the less specific DNS alternative in the sample ranking.

questions.question: What happens when the agent calls argocd_rollback without an approver?
options: The event is recorded but blocked with "blocked: no slack approval"
The rollback executes because argocd_rollback is a read-only tool
The call is silently omitted from the audit log
The agent retries until an approver appears
questions.explanation: argocd_rollback is in destructive_tools. Without approver, call leaves executed false and returns the explicit no-Slack-approval block result.

questions.question: What result follows the second rollback call when the demo passes approver="alice@sre"?
options: blocked: unknown tool
executed by alice@sre, with approved and executed set true
ok (read-only), with approved still false
blocked: no slack approval, because the first call was denied
questions.explanation: A supplied approver satisfies the destructive-tool gate; the event records alice@sre and both approved and executed become true.

questions.question: What does the audit log retain about a denied destructive command?
options: Only successful read-only calls are retained
The command is executed but marked approved=false
The considered command is retained with executed=false and its block result
The command is discarded unless an approver later authorizes it
questions.explanation: Agent.call creates and appends an AuditEvent before returning, so even a denied call remains traceable with considered=true, executed=false, and its result.

questions.question: Why can the agent query Prometheus before proposing a rollback?
options: promql is treated as destructive but has a built-in approval
all tools are allowed until the first hypothesis is ranked
the graph bypasses tool policy for telemetry reads
promql is in read_only_tools, while rollback tools are kept in destructive_tools
questions.explanation: The tool policy explicitly executes promql, logql, and related telemetry reads without approval, while argocd_rollback requires a human approver.
